Class DrawUtil

java.lang.Object
DrawUtil
public class DrawUtil extends Object
A static utility class containing convenient methods for drawing, such as for drawing various shapes to a Graphics2D object.

    • drawText

      public static void drawText(Graphics2D g, Vector2 pos, String text, Vector2 justify)
      Draws a given string of text using a specified text justify.
      Parameters:
      g - The Graphics2D object to which to render the shape
      pos - The position of the text
      text - The string to draw
      justify - A vector representing the justify of the string, which defines where in the text position refers to. Each component represents the multiple of the text's size in that direction. For example, for the position to refer to the top left corner, the vector <0, 0> should be used; for the center, <0.5, 0.5>; for the bottom right corner, <1, 1>.

    • getInfiniteLineEndpoints

      public static Vector2[] getInfiniteLineEndpoints(Vector2 pos, Vector2 direction, Vector2 screenDimensions)
      Calculates the end points used for rendering an infinitely long line.
      Parameters:
      pos - A vector representing a point that the line passes through
      direction - The direction vector of the line
      screenDimensions - A vector representing the dimensions of the screen
      Returns:
      An array with two elements, each representing an endpoint of the line. The two endpoints are ordered based on the direction vector.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if direction is equal to the zero vector

    • drawDirectionVector

      public static void drawDirectionVector(Graphics2D g, Point position, Vector2 vector, Color color, int width, int length, float fullyOpaqueLength)
      Draws the outline of a vector, with the opacity decreasing linearly when the vector's length is less than a specified value. However, the vector will always be drawn to have a constant length. This method is useful for highlighting the direction of a vector, such as in visualizing the net electric field.
      Parameters:
      g - The Graphics2D object to which to render the shape
      position - The screen-space position of the tail of the vector
      vector - The world-space vector to draw (NOTE: the positive y-axis is up)
      color - The color using which to draw the vector
      width - The width using which to draw the vector
      length - The length using which to draw the vector
      fullyOpaqueLength - The minimum length at which the vector will be drawn at full opacity

    • drawMagnitudeVector

      public static void drawMagnitudeVector(Graphics2D g, Point position, Vector2 vector, Color color, int maxWidth, float maxWidthLength)
      Fills in a vector, with the displayed vector's length reflecting the vector's length and the width decreasing linearly when the length is less than a specified value. This method is useful for highlighting the magnitude of a vector, such as in displaying forces applied to an object.
      Parameters:
      g - The Graphics2D object to which to render the shape
      position - The screen-space position of the tail of the vector
      vector - The world-space vector to draw (NOTE: the positive y-axis is up)
      color - The color using which to draw the vector
      maxWidth - The maximum width of the drawn vector
      maxWidthLength - The minimum length at which the vector will be drawn at its maximum width

    • drawDirectionVectorZ

      public static void drawDirectionVectorZ(Graphics2D g, Point position, float z, Color color, float radius, float fullyOpaqueLength)
      Visualizes the z-component of a 3D vector using dots and crosses, with the opacity decreasing linearly when the z-component is less than a specified value. This method also draws the dot/cross with circle surrounding it. This method is used for highlighting the direction of a vector, such as in visualizing the net magnetic field.
      Parameters:
      g - The Graphics2D object to which to render the shape
      position - The screen-space position at which to draw the vector
      z - The world-space vector to draw (NOTE: the positive z-axis is out of the screen)
      color - The color using which to draw the vector
      radius - The radius using which to draw the vector
      fullyOpaqueLength - The minimum length at which the vector will be drawn at full opacity

    • drawDotCross

      public static void drawDotCross(Graphics2D g, Point point, float radius)
      Draws a dot or a cross with a specified radius, used to represent the z-component of a 3D vector. If radius is positive, a dot will be drawn; otherwise, a cross will be drawn. The dots/crosses are designed to be able to fit within a circle with the magnitude of the specified radius.
      Parameters:
      g - The Graphics2D object to which to render the shape
      point - The screen-space position at which to draw the vector
      radius - The radius of a circle surrounding the shape. The radius should have the same sign as the z-component in world space of a vector being represented. If radius > 0, a dot will be drawn; otherwise, a cross will be drawn. The magnitude of radius is used to determine the size of a surrounding circle.
